name: Space motion sickness - first flight
note: first Shuttle flight: 30% mild, 24% moderate, 13% severe

name: Space motion sickness - repeat flight
note: lower incidence on a second flight, not significant; the abstract gives no rate
population: Shuttle crewmembers with a second flight

name: Headache reports in NASA CO2 association study
note: 19 of 49 astronauts, Expeditions 2-31; CO2 level was associated with headache reports, causation not shown; a later prospective study (24 astronauts) found no link with CO2

name: Skin rash / hypersensitivity
note: includes hypersensitivity, tinea versicolor, dermatitis, rosacea
population: 46 long-duration ISS crew missions (41 US astronauts)

name: Upper respiratory symptoms
note: prolonged congestion, rhinitis and sneezing: symptom events, not confirmed infections
population: 46 long-duration ISS crew missions (41 US astronauts)

name: Upper respiratory symptoms
note: prolonged congestion, rhinitis, sneezing; earlier cohort

name: Skin infection
note: skin infections including pus-forming wounds; observed events, not a share of astronauts
population: 46 long-duration ISS crew missions (41 US astronauts)

name: Herpes zoster
note: no herpes zoster events in ISS Expeditions 1-28/29 (small sample, not zero risk); cold sores are row HSV

name: HSV-related cold sores / herpesvirus events
note: cold sores (usually HSV-1), not herpes zoster (VZV); both cohorts report 6 events
population: 46 long-duration ISS crew missions (41 US astronauts)

name: Early optic-disc-edema findings associated with SANS
note: about 70% of ISS crew on 4-6 month missions show early signs; not severe disease, not the probability of a diagnosis for one astronaut
detail: optic disc edema / increased total retinal thickness
